costAxis.description: One axis of a Word's charged-cost bound. `class` is a sound upper bound on how the charge grows with the Word's input; `exact` records that some contribution provably attains that class, distinguishing a bound known to be tight from one that is merely safe.

valueDependent.description: Present when the charge on this axis also grows with the term count of an algebraic operand, which `class` — counted in elements — cannot see: `MUL` is `const` in elements, yet two 16-term operands charge 262,144 units of numericWork where two rationals charge 1. `scripts/check-value-dependent-cost.mjs` sets this by measurement, so it is present exactly when the charge grows across a rational, a 7-term and a 16-term operand. Budget such a Word from a small run's `resourceUsage.algebraicTerms`, not from its class alone.

cost.description: The Word's charged cost on the three metered resources the runtime counts (`executionSteps` / `numericWork` / `collectionWork`). Declared per axis so a caller can bound a phrase before running it: the axes join pointwise under concatenation, so a phrase's bound is the join of its Words' bounds.

projection.description: The conditions under which a well-formed operand yields a reasoned NIL. `when` accepts a list because a Word can project for more than one reason: `POW` answers NIL both for a zero base under a negative exponent and for an exponent that leaves the exact field. `reason` already accepted a list; a single condition may still be written as a bare string. As with `errorWhen`, a condition here names a state of the input rather than an outcome; this field is what says the outcome is a projection.

family.description: The semantic family the Word selects its shared laws from. The Words that act on numbers and on what two sources agree on divide along two orders: `knowledgeOrder` is the order of what is known of a value — the arithmetic, graded by zero shapes, and RECONCILE — every member citing LANG.VALUES.SHAPE; `truthOrder` is FALSE < UNKNOWN < TRUE — the truth values, their connectives and the Words that ask an order — every member citing LANG.VALUES.TRUTH.

operands.description: What the Word does with each operand, first-pushed first (LANG.FAILURE.PASSTHROUGH). `leaf`: the Word reads it as one value that is not a container — a Scalar, String, Boolean or Symbol — so an absent operand makes the result that absence, and a Vector or Record there lifts the Word over its elements (LANG.COLLECTIONS.LIFT). `data`: the Word reads it whole, so an absent operand makes the result that absence. `element`: the Word carries it without reading it, so a NIL is an ordinary value. `control`: a block it evaluates, a name it binds, defines or looks up, or a message it raises, so a NIL there is malformed use. `truth`: read in truth position, where a NIL is UNKNOWN (LANG.VALUES.TRUTH), and which lifts like a `leaf`. Present exactly when `inputs` is a fixed count, with one role per operand.

domains.description: The value domains (LANG.VALUES.DISJOINT) of each operand and result, first-pushed first. An operand's entry names what the Word reads there: for a `leaf` or `truth` operand, the domain of one lane, since a Vector or Record there lifts the Word over its elements (LANG.COLLECTIONS.LIFT); for any other role, the whole value. A result's entry names what the Word answers when every operand is in its declared domain and nothing is lifted; a NIL the Word projects is declared by `projection`, not here. Present exactly when both `inputs` and `outputs` are fixed counts, with one entry per operand and per result. Read by the fused route, which runs a Word inside a block only when its domains stay within scalars and Booleans.

errorWhen.description: The conditions under which the Word raises. A condition names a state of the *input* — "the divisor is zero", "the index is outside the vector" — and not an outcome, so the schema permits the same name in one Word's `errorWhen` and another's `projection.when`. Which field it appears in is what decides the outcome, per Word, and the two are never both declared for one condition on one Word. No condition is currently declared both ways anywhere in the registry: `indexOutOfBounds` was the last one that was — `GET` projected it while `TAKE` and `PUT` raised it — and those two now project it too, so every condition in the registry has one outcome across the whole vocabulary.

partiality.description: A summary of the declared outcomes, never a choice of its own (scripts/check-word-schema-migration.mjs derives it): `projecting` when the Word declares a projection; else `partial` when it runs a block (purity `conditional`) or declares an errorWhen condition spec/outcomes.json marks `repair: program`; else `total` — it raises only on an operand of the wrong kind.

field.description: Whether the Word keeps numbers inside the field (LANG.CONTRACT.FIELD): `closed` when every number it answers lies in the field whenever every number it reads does, `leaving` when it can answer one of the two points over zero (`1/0`, `0/0`) from operands that hold none. Only the total operations that reach past the field are `leaving` — `DIV` (`1 0 DIV`), `POW` (`0 -1 POW`) and `NUM` (`'1/0' NUM`); a Word that only carries, orders or rounds numbers is `closed`, and a Word that runs a block is `closed` itself, the block's own Words deciding for it. `rust/src/field_closure_laws.rs` holds one witness per `leaving` Word and runs every `closed` arithmetic Word over finite operands.

domain.description: One of the seven disjoint domains of LANG.VALUES.DISJOINT, or `any` for a position that takes every domain.

domainSet.description: One domain, or a list of two or more when a position takes several.
